steps.observation: You have 900 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
# DNA vs RNA: Key Differences

## Structure
- **DNA** – Double-stranded helix; very stable
- **RNA** – Single-stranded; more flexible and less stable

## Sugar
- **DNA** – Contains **deoxyribose** (missing one oxygen atom)
- **RNA** – Contains **ribose** (has the extra -OH group)

## Bases
- Both use Adenine, Guanine, Cytosine
- **DNA** uses **Thymine (T)**
- **RNA** uses **Uracil (U)** instead

## Location
- **DNA** – Mainly in the **nucleus** (also mitochondria/chloroplasts)
- **RNA** – Made in the nucleus, works throughout the **cell**

## Function
- **DNA** – Long-term **storage** of genetic information
- **RNA** – **Carries and executes** instructions from DNA

## Types of RNA
- **mRNA** – Messenger; carries the genetic code to ribosomes
- **tRNA** – Transfer; brings amino acids during protein synthesis
- **rRNA** – Ribosomal; forms part of the ribosome itself

## Simple Analogy
> DNA is the **master blueprint** locked in an office. RNA is the **working copy** taken to the construction site.

---

Time used: well under 900 seconds ✓
